reports.title: REPORT OF FOREIGN PRIVATE ISSUER PURSUANT TO RULE 13a-16 OR 15d-16 OF THE

desk.headline: Revenue down 5% to $263.1m, slightly above estimates, but loss of $0.13 a share was wider than expected; Q4 and 2027 EBITDA seen flat despite losing the Prospector 5 rig
results: Revenue fell 5% from a year ago to $263.1m (up 13% from the June quarter) as dayrate revenue slipped to $216.8m from $241.0m; Southeast Asia sales dropped to $51.9m from $80.6m.
Rig running costs rose a third to $170.5m, so the company swung to a $38.7m loss from a $27.8m profit a year earlier.
Adjusted EBITDA jumped 80% from the June quarter to $78.9m as rigs that changed contracts in Q2 went back to work.
Nine new contracts since August add about $269m of work, including putting the idle rig Hild to work offshore Nigeria.
Cash fell to $202.6m from $379.7m at the start of the year, mostly after buying five rigs in January; total borrowings are $2.53bn.

guidance.summary: No figures, only direction: Q4 adjusted EBITDA is expected to be roughly the same as Q3 even after losing Prospector 5, and 2027 EBITDA broadly in line with 2026, with a weaker first quarter and a strong pick-up late in the year.

call.source: No call coverage found (call held 19 Nov 2026, 09:00 New York time); CEO comments in the press release are reflected in guidance and watch points

watch: Prospector 5, which sank off Gabon on 24 Oct with four people confirmed dead: the $200m insurance payment due 24 Nov, investigation findings and any claims.
Whether 2027 contract coverage climbs from 52%, with the company pointing to more work in Southeast Asia and West Africa.
Cash and debt: interest costs on $2.53bn of borrowings against cash of $202.6m.
